key_claims: Knee osteoarthritis develops as cartilage gradually breaks down, causing pain and stiffness.
Weak leg muscles and being overweight or obese increase risk for knee osteoarthritis.
Eating more plants and less processed or sugary food reduces inflammation and can reduce pain from osteoarthritis.
Losing 10 pounds can reduce stress on the knees by 40 pounds with every step.
Regular physical activity and maintaining a healthy weight may lower risk of developing osteoarthritis.
Family history of osteoarthritis does not mean a person will inevitably develop it.
limitations: The source is an expert opinion piece, not a systematic review or clinical trial.
Specific statistics on prevalence and risk factors are not detailed.
The effectiveness of lifestyle changes is described generally without quantified outcomes.
The source does not provide comparative data on different treatments.
what_not_to_say: The source does not claim that lifestyle changes can reverse osteoarthritis.
The source does not specify that running is definitively protective against knee osteoarthritis.
The source does not provide evidence that diet alone can prevent osteoarthritis.
The source does not quantify the reduction in risk from exercise or weight loss.
